HOW BEHAVIOUR AND COMM SCORES x YOUR TRUE MMR SCORE
15 Aug, 2024 @ 10:14pm
Bitshop
If the Dota community wants to bring politics into the talk, then let's have a little talk about the DISCIPLINE and HONOUR of competing in the Olympic sports because I believe that has something related to the Dota e-Sports too. Good and important moral values for e-gamers to learn more!

Competing with your true integrity and reputation carries your honour (respect). Otherwise, you may be disqualified or not legit to be known as a legal competitor among humanity for true justice.

What and how to understand fair competition especially when you are a Dota player who competes for a beautiful MMR also? If you are carrying a lower MMR and competing in the Ranked MM, you may still have more graceful honour (respect) compared to some who are carrying higher MMR because their honour (respect) may be less graceful than yours, or vice-versa. This is all about the story of how you show your discipline to the rules of the Dota 2 game when you are striving for that MMR score.

If you read an Olympic Paris 2024 news (link: https://www.reddit.com/r/trackandfield/comments/1ckmw5j/usa_got_disqualified_because_they_changed/ ) to explain how embarrassing it can be when you appear in a WORLD with much of competitions which are set by rules/laws, and you must fully respecting the rules/laws too! - Otherwise, you can lose your full honour (respect) by the community of Dota or the world of MOBA gamers if you are proud to "big talking" with your high MMR. TBH, I always have high confidence when speaking or voicing up in this community because I believe that I never break any rules which are set for the great competitive "World Leaderboard" of the Dota 2 games. - Why are so many rules breakers always hiding behind their "duplicated Steam accounts" when they want to make unreasonable complaints to cover up their failures in the Dota 2 games?

Besides the VAC status that works for all Steam users, I guess someday, the Steam account should have a publication for the "greenlight" scores of the Dota players.

Thanks for reading and understanding.
